body:
- Set the version to 0.3.1, tag v0.3.1 so the release workflow builds the binaries, and publish the crate to crates.io
- Brings the command sandbox, the step-limit and repeat fixes, the streaming fixes and the Colab notebook to people who install the latest release
title: Release 0.3.1

body:
- At most once a day, check the latest GitHub release in the background, with a short timeout, so startup never waits on the network
- In the TUI, when a newer version exists, ask: "openbatrangs X is available (you have Y). Install it now? y/n"; on y, run the release installer into the folder of the running binary and ask for a restart
- In one-shot mode, print one line about the new version at the end, with no prompt
- Add `openbatrangs update` to update on demand
- Turn the check off with `--no-update-check` or `OPENBATRANGS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`
title: Check for new releases and offer to install them

body:
- The prompt says never to ask the user, and a question in place of an answer is rejected by the finish gate, so the loop forces the model to continue
- Add an `ask_user` tool that ends the turn and shows the question
- In the TUI, the next message answers it and continues the same conversation; in one-shot mode, print the question and exit
title: Let the model ask the user a question

body:
- Asking for example code, such as reading a directory recursively, makes the agent list the workspace instead of answering
- The native system prompt requires a tool call in every reply and says to list directories before assuming a layout
- `requires_file_work` matches words such as "write ", "add ", "fix " and "tests" in the task, and then rejects any finish that wrote no files
- Rewrite the prompt so questions that do not need the workspace get a direct answer
- Remove the keyword gate; require a passing check only after the model changed files in a project with a build or test setup
title: Answer questions directly instead of forcing tool calls

body:
- Cache each block's rendered lines for the current width
- Keep running line heights and draw only the blocks on screen
- Move old blocks to the session file on disk and load them back when scrolled to
- Test with 10,000 blocks and check that memory stays bounded
title: Draw only the visible part of the transcript

body:
- Parse replies with pulldown-cmark
- Style headings, bold and italics, inline code, lists, quotes, links, rules and tables
- Highlight fenced code with syntect in every message, however long the session
title: Render Markdown in replies

body:
- Fold each step to one line: step number, title, model and time taken
- Take the title from the model's own heading, or the first sentence of its reasoning
- Show the thinking, the decision and one line per tool call inside an open step; open those to see the full reasoning, arguments and output
- Fold with a click, or move between the input and the transcript with Tab, between blocks with arrow keys, and fold with Enter or Space
- Keep the running step open and fold finished steps automatically

Depends on #24.
title: Fold agent steps in the TUI transcript

body:
- Rebuild the native and JSON step loops as `loop { state = match state { ... } }`, one small function per state
- Send structured events to the reporter: step started, reasoning, tool call, tool result, answer, finished
- Keep the one-shot CLI output unchanged
title: Run the agent loops as a state machine with structured events
